comments.text: My wife and I needed a new car after I totaled my 2dr altima. We had a baby on the way neither of us had proof of employment she had like a 540 credit score we got a 2021 Toyota Camry with $6000 down for about $22k she got approved for financing without proof of anything at 24% APR a year later. After I got her credit score up to 720+ we refinanced through USAA at 5.5% after another year I paid off her car completely and also bought myself a 2012 fully loaded Kia optima for $6800 cash. Her credit score now floats around 799-802. The point of this story is sometimes you just take what you can get and work hard and you will see results. Of course we could have gotten a used car for under $6000 but I wanted her to have something safe and reliable for her and the new baby and we were paying out of pocket for a rental car so it wasn’t practical to do a lot of car shopping. Because each day was costing us $60.  Sometimes you have to take the high APR and make payments to get your credit up so you can refinance. I know not a lot of people do what we did. We could have just paid $500 a month for 72 months and paid 20k extra for the car but I hate making payments to the bank. From now on I will only either lease or buy cash. Also we built credit by opening up a credit card and using it for purchases then paying down the balance every month. You’d be surprised how fast you can build your credit making on time payments.

comments.author: @lmrbeerbellyl
comments.text: They're able to roll-over negative equity in a much more expensive vehicle because the negative equity will end representing a much lower percentage of the loan than it would on a cheaper vehicle.  This is an easy concept to understand....  If you trade in a car with $5000 negative equity and try to get a loan on a $10,000 car the negative equity would represent 33% of the total loan.  If you rolled over the same negative equity into a $95,000 car the negative equity would only represent 2% of the loan.   A bank is never going to write the loan first car, but they will write the loan on the second car provided the buyer meets the other requirements (income, credit score, etc).
